record.context_brief: Large ordinals inside scattered semi-Eberlein compacta
record.original_question: Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compact space contain a copy of the ordinal interval [0,ω₂]?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.7. Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum contain a copy of [0, ω2]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. All spaces are Hausdorff. A compact space $K$ is called Eberlein compact if it is homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space. More generally, $K$ is called semi-Eberlein if there exists a set $D \subseteq K$ such that:
(i) $D$ is dense in $K$, and
(ii) $D$ is homeomorphic to a subset of a $\Sigma$-product of real lines $\Sigma(\mathbb{R}^\Gamma) = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^\Gamma : \{\gamma \in \Gamma : x(\gamma) \neq 0\}\text{ is countable}\}$ for some index set $\Gamma$, in such a way that $D$ sits inside the $\sigma$-product $\sigma(\mathbb{R}^\Gamma) = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^\Gamma : \{\gamma \in \Gamma : x(\gamma) \neq 0\}\text{ is finite}\}$ (equivalently, $K$ embeds in some $[0,1]^\Gamma$ in a way that the points with finite support form a dense subset).

A compact space $K$ is scattered if every nonempty closed subset of $K$ has an isolated point. For an ordinal $\alpha$, the ordinal interval $[0,\alpha]$ is regarded as a compact space with the order topology.

Question. Does there exist a scattered semi-Eberlein compact space $K$ which contains a topological copy of the ordinal interval $[0, \omega_2]$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on norming Markushevich bases (2024). Web searches did not surface any subsequent paper resolving it; related work (e.g., on scattered Eberlein compacta and on hyperspaces of semi-Eberlein compacta) does not address whether $[0,\omega_2]$ can embed in a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum. It therefore appears to remain open.
